I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize system this year. In Quzhou County, that is the crop pattern I trust most because I know how to manage it, the buyers know it, and the risk is lower than trying something unfamiliar at my age. I will plant winter wheat on the main land first, then follow it with summer maize on the same fields after wheat harvest. I will not spread myself across too many crops, because that makes labor, irrigation, fertilizer, and pest control harder to manage. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed for stable yield, put most fertilizer on nitrogen but still keep phosphorus and potassium in the plan so the land does not weaken, irrigate several times because our area can turn dry, and keep pesticide use limited to the main disease and insect pressure instead of spraying too often. For wheat I will use rotary tillage to prepare a firm seedbed; after wheat harvest I will move quickly into no-tillage summer maize to save moisture and time.
